portal_hypertension.abstract: Chronic liver disease is an increasingly prevalent and heterogeneous syndrome with important consequences for cardiovascular function. As the global burdens of chronic liver disease and cirrhosis continue to rise, cardiovascular disease has emerged as a major driver of overall morbidity and mortality in affected patients. Despite the growing recognition of the intersectionality between hepatology and cardiology care clinically, cardiovascular disease risk among patients with liver disease is underrecognized. This state-of-the-art review summarizes the current understanding of the bidirectional interactions between the liver and the cardiovascular system. Shared mechanisms-including inflammat...

portal_hypertension.abstract: Baveno VII criteria prioritize Liver Stiffness Measurement (LSM) for portal hypertension risk stratification, primarily using transient elastography. We aimed to evaluate two-dimensional-shear wave elastography (2D-SWE) cutoffs, assess the etiology-dependent utility of spleen stiffness (SSM), and introduce a novel Combined Hepato-splenic Stiffness Index (CHSSI). This ambispective, observational study enrolled 100 chronic liver disease patients. Participants underwent 2D-SWE for LSM and SSM, alongside endoscopy as the reference standard. portal_hypertension.abstract: Gastroesophageal varices are recognized complications of Fontan-associated liver disease, but clinically significant varices have generally been reported more than 10 years after Fontan completion. The mechanisms of early variceal formation remain unclear. We report a child with tricuspid atresia who developed isolated gastric varices approximately 7 years after extracardiac Fontan completion in the presence of a pre-existing gastro-renal shunt (GRS). The patient underwent bidirectional Glenn palliation at 9 months of age.
